skills.title: Client email intake
skills.summary: Find the client and deal by the sender's email (on the CRM if your organisation has one, otherwise on Monday), save the attachments to the deal folder and register them on the deal.
skills.details: For the email you choose, the assistant finds the client and deal on your organisation's CRM by the sender's email address (without a CRM, the Deal on Monday), finds or creates the deal folder with its tmp/ folder, saves the attachments not there yet into tmp/ and registers them on the deal. It reads the email from the mail account you added on this computer; only with the enterprise shared mailbox and no mail account here does the app's server read it and copy the attachments into tmp/ on OneDrive. A missing client or deal is created only when you confirm it, and it asks you to choose when the sender matches several clients or deals. It doesn't rename files, change Monday, reply to the email or mark it as read.
examples: Process this email and save the files to the deal
Save the documents the client sent in this email to the deal

skills.title: Check loan documents
skills.summary: Check a client's documents against the 23-item checklist and report what needs doing; with the CRM, process a deal's new files from any source and file the ones that pass.
skills.details: The assistant checks the source file (genuine issued copy, edited, photo or scan), recognises the type, reads it by that type's rules and cross-checks the documents; the report gives the conclusion, Fact Find details and what to tell the client. With the CRM, when you ask it to process a deal it takes each new file in the deal's tmp/ (client portal, email, your upload, OneDrive): it registers each file with its type and client, records the results, marks a required document received only when fully met and files each document that passes. Then it lists what needs your review: notes the client will see, documents with open items and likely duplicates. It accepts a document only when you say so and never copies TFNs, Medicare or card numbers.
examples: What's new for the Whitmore deal?
Has any client sent new documents?
Check the payslip and statement I just attached

skills.title: Australian business lookup (ABN)
skills.summary: Look up an ABN, ACN or business name: active or cancelled, GST, and whether it matches the name on the document.
skills.details: The assistant looks up the business on the Australian Business Register's ABN Lookup, gives the entity name, entity type, ABN status (active or cancelled, and since when), GST and business names, then lists what needs action: a cancelled ABN, a wrong ABN number, or a business name that differs from the document (allowing for trust names and sole traders' names). A printout or screenshot of an ABN Lookup result sent by the client is looked up again, not used as evidence. Registration status with ASIC (whether a company has been deregistered) isn't in the ABR, so the assistant says clearly that it couldn't check it. The assistant never guesses business details from memory.
examples: Is ABC Pty Ltd still active?
